_help: Launch Readiness Checklist. Each check has a category, a weight (points) and a why line. Yes gives full points, Partly half, No none. reportUrl is the link of the Get the full Launch Readiness Report button: replace the placeholder # with the real page or form. Grades are by score out of 100.
reportLabel: Get the full Launch Readiness Report
reportLine: A detailed review of your launch plan, with fixes for each gap.

checks.text: Total supply and allocation are final and written down
checks.why: Changing the split after launch breaks trust.

checks.text: Team and investor tokens have a cliff and vesting
checks.why: Unlocked insider tokens are the top worry for buyers.

checks.text: The token has a clear use in the product
checks.why: A token with no job struggles to hold attention.

checks.text: The unlock schedule is public
checks.why: People plan around big unlocks. Surprises hurt.

checks.text: Circulating supply at launch is known and published
checks.why: Exchanges and data sites ask for it on day one.

checks.text: A lawyer has reviewed the token and the sale in your main countries
checks.why: Token rules differ a lot between countries.

checks.text: The project has a legal entity
checks.why: Exchanges, banks and partners need someone to sign with.

checks.text: Terms of use and a privacy policy are live
checks.why: Basic protection for you and your users.

checks.text: Countries you will block are decided and enforced
checks.why: Some countries restrict token sales or need licences.

checks.text: Investor, advisor and KOL agreements are signed
checks.why: Handshake deals turn into disputes.

checks.text: Smart contracts are audited and the report is public
checks.why: Unaudited contracts are a common way funds get lost.

checks.text: Treasury and admin keys use a multisig
checks.why: One stolen key should not drain the project.

checks.text: Admin powers (mint, pause, upgrade) are listed publicly
checks.why: Hidden powers look like a rug risk.

checks.text: There is a bug bounty or a way to report bugs
checks.why: Friendly hackers need a way to reach you.

checks.text: Team accounts use two-factor login with security keys or an app
checks.why: Hacked socials are used to post scam links.

checks.text: There is an active community channel with moderators
checks.why: Launch day questions need fast, real answers.

checks.text: Official links are pinned everywhere
checks.why: Scammers copy projects with fake links on launch day.

checks.text: Moderators know the team never DMs first
checks.why: Fake support DMs are a common scam.

checks.text: Docs or an FAQ explain the product and the token
checks.why: Saves your team answering the same question 500 times.

checks.text: Early users and testers are thanked or rewarded
checks.why: Your first fans become your loudest voices.

checks.text: Launch date and plan are shared in advance
checks.why: A surprise launch looks rushed.

checks.text: Paid promotions are clearly disclosed
checks.why: Hidden ads can break advertising rules and trust.

checks.text: There is a press or media kit (logo, short story, links)
checks.why: Makes it easy for others to write about you.

checks.text: Posts are scheduled for launch week
checks.why: Launch week is busy. Prepare posts before.

checks.text: No messaging promises prices or returns
checks.why: Price promises bring legal risk and angry holders.

checks.text: The liquidity plan (amount, pairs, venues) is decided
checks.why: Thin liquidity means wild price swings.

checks.text: Liquidity pool tokens are locked or held by a multisig
checks.why: Removable liquidity is the classic rug pull.

checks.text: Any market maker deal is written and its terms understood
checks.why: Bad market maker deals can drain tokens.

checks.text: Data sites (CoinGecko, CoinMarketCap) applications are ready
checks.why: Listings on data sites help people find you.

checks.text: Treasury has runway outside your own token
checks.why: If your token drops, you still need to pay the team.

grades.label: Ready for launch
grades.line: Strong foundations. Close the last gaps and go.

grades.label: Nearly ready
grades.line: Good base, but a few gaps could hurt on launch day.

grades.label: Not yet
grades.line: Important pieces are missing. Fix the biggest gaps first.

grades.label: Early days
grades.line: Lots to do before launch. That is normal: start from the top of the gaps list.
